content:
I really like verso-blueprint — but I hit a snag: when I convert the generated HTML to PDF with WeasyPrint, the PDF outline comes out scrambled. After a fair bit of digging I traced it back to verso-blueprint itself: when a blueprint node links a Lean structure/class/inductive, the Fields/Methods/Constructors/Extends sub-section labels get emitted as literal top-level <h1>s — regardless of how deeply the node is nested — so each page ends up with several out-of-order <h1>s. That's what corrupts the outline (and PDF bookmarks, and screen-reader heading nav).

Before declaring it a real bug rather than something I'd misconfigured, I tracked it down to the exact source: a hard-coded <h1> in renderTitledSection? (plus a second one for Extends) in ExternalDeclRender.lean. To rule out a fluke on my end, I had Claude write a little crawler that scans deployed blueprints for the signature. It reproduces on 3 of the 4 reference blueprints (Sphere Packing, Noperthedron, Verso FLT; Carleson is clean only because it doesn't link any structure/class/inductive with sub-sections).

Full write-up, root cause, and the checker: https://github.com/leanprover/verso-blueprint/issues/130
